newsitem.title: USA: LatAm telecom stocks boom on funds, good news.
newsitem.headline: LatAm telecom stocks boom on funds, good news.

text.p: Latin American telephone companies are surging on Wall Street these days as once-burned international investors look at the region anew, analysts said.
Since the start of the year, Latin America's six big telecommunications shares have outpaced even the record-setting Dow Jones Industrial Average.
As of Wednesday they had risen an average of 23.2 percent on the New York Stock Exchange, according to Morgan Stanley's Capital International index.
By contrast, the major stock markets in the region have gone up almost 18 percent and the Dow Jones Industrial Average is up 8.4 percent on the year.
Analysts said the boom arose in part from good news from Latin America, and fund managers pouring some of their hundreds of billions of dollars into bargain-priced Latin American stocks.

Eduardo Cabrera, Merrill Lynch's chief Latin American strategist, said such American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) as Brazil's Telebras and Telefonos de Mexico were benefiting from "the tremendous amount of money that is flowing into mutual funds ... and moving into Latin America."
He added, "It has been extremely important that Argentine (telecoms), Telmex and Telebras have rallied because it is indicative of the big money that has come into the region."

State-run Telebras heads the telecom pack. Cheered on by analysts encouraged by the reformist government's moves to privatise the company, its shares have risen 28 percent since the start of the year. They were off 75 cents at $97.125 at midday Thursday.
Besides Telebras and Telmex, the other major telecoms are Telefonica de Argentina, Telecom Argentina, Compania de Telecomunicaciones de Chile and Telefonica del Peru.
Analysts said the telecoms' surge marked the return to Latin America of fund managers who had fled the region's markets after Mexico's fiscal collapse in late 1994.
Telecommunications shares that trade in New York as ADRs, with their volume, reliability and ease of purchase, are favourites for Latin American portfolios.
"These being the most liquid stocks, they are going to feel the flows (of capital) the most," said Leslie Marcus, Latin American telecommunications analyst at Santander Investment.
"If someone wants exposure to Brazil they are going to buy Telebras. In Argentina, the same thing."

The ADRs also are seen as generating attractive earnings. Economic growth in the region over the next few years is expected to be twice that of United States and companies have great chances to expand as underserved consumers buy telephones.
Telebras, for example, "is a company that can grow earnings above 20 percent a year for the foreseeable future," said Luiz Carvalho, Latin American telecommunications analyst for Morgan Stanley.
Latin American telecoms are trading at about five times earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization. By contrast, Asian telecoms trade at about three times that level.
Matthew Hickman, an analyst at Lehman Brothers, said Latin American telecoms were "a dirt cheap sector, and especially when you compare them to Asian telecoms they are very cheap."
The shares also have been helped by good news from the companies themselves and their home countries that markets have applauded, such as Argentina reajusting its basic telephone rates.
And Telmex, the one-time state monopoly, started the year at $33 a share and was trading at $39.375 on Thursday despite the launch of long-distance competition and disappointing 1996 earnings.
